Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

I've written `/workspace/result.json`. The shipped total for 1 March to 31 May 2025 (UTC) is **9,329,707 cents**, across **407** distinct orders.

| Region | Cents |
|---|---|
| north | 2,666,579 |
| south | 2,714,624 |
| east | 1,671,579 |
| west | 2,276,925 |

`duplicates_skipped` is 20. The by-region values add up to the total, and the file has exactly the requested keys.

**How I computed it:**
- I read all 30 pages: 1,500 listings, of which 1,480 are distinct orders.
- All 20 repeated listings were identical to the first copy, so which copy I kept doesn't matter.
- Every order has one of the four documented statuses, so the exact "shipped" match had no odd variants to catch. 760 of the 1,480 distinct orders are shipped, and 407 of those fall in the date range.
- Timestamps were converted to UTC before the range check, with the end bound at 1 June 00:00 UTC, exclusive.
- Each order was discounted and rounded half up to the cent individually, then summed.
- I looked up each of the 117 customers once and kept the result. None returned a 404.

**What I noticed in the data:** nothing unusual. The service did throw some errors along the way: 13 rate-limit responses, which I waited out as instructed, and 12 expired tokens, where I fetched a new token and repeated the request. No page or customer was skipped or guessed.

My working script is in `/tmp/recon`, outside the workspace.
